name: Microsoft COCO (Common Objects in Context)
description: MS COCO is a large-scale dataset of everyday scenes emphasizing non-iconic object views, contextual co-occurrence, and precise instance-level segmentation: 328k images with 2.5M labeled instances across 91 common ‘thing’ categories (82 with >5k instances), with rich context (avg. 3.5 categories and 7.7 instances per image) and per-instance masks and bounding boxes, plus five captions per image.
citeAs: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár. Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context. arXiv:1405.0312v3, 21 Feb 2015. (Abridged version in ECCV 2014).

creator.name: Microsoft COCO authors (Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár) with affiliations including Cornell Tech, TTI-Chicago, Facebook AI Research, Microsoft Research, Brown University, Caltech, UC Irvine

rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollection: Images sourced mainly from Flickr using object-object and object-scene query pairs to prioritize non-iconic scenes; limited per-photographer sampling and explicit filtering to remove iconic images; near-duplicates removed and images grouped by photographer/date to manage splits; only ‘thing’ categories initially (no ‘stuff’).
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT), with custom UIs for hierarchical category labeling, instance spotting, instance segmentation, and segmentation verification; additional caption annotations (five per image).
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataUseCases: Designed for object detection and precise instance segmentation in natural, contextual scenes; evaluation and baseline analysis for bounding-box detection and segmentation-from-detections; supports research on non-iconic views, contextual reasoning, 2D localization, and captioning.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Images are from Flickr and may contain people; dataset includes many segmented person instances and faces are listed among candidate categories, but no discussion of consent, privacy handling, or PII mitigation is provided.
